correctness.rationale: For every prime \(p\mid N\), reduction U_N→F_p^× is an onto group map with equal fibers. Fourier inversion of the elementary-symmetric subset enumerator gives exactly two counts, differing by \((-1)^r B_{p,m}(r)\). The finite geometric product identity holds for p=2 as well as odd primes. Every coefficient B in degrees \(0\) through \(\varphi(N)\) is a positive bounded-composition count, so uniformity modulo N is contradicted after projection for every r. The proof includes all endpoints. The standalone DP checks 95 moduli and all their relevant prime divisors/cardinalities/residues but is supportive finite evidence only.

Gaitanas (2023), Theorem 1.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.14141: uniformity of *all nonempty subset sums pooled* for odd N, a theorem in the opposite granularity.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the contiguous-integer criterion nor pooled-nonempty equidistribution implies exact signed counts at each cardinality for the unit system modulo all composite moduli. The 1994 prime-instance nonuniformity is weaker than the exact all-moduli coefficient theorem. A general character enumerator could dominate this result if an explicit unit-system coefficient evaluation is found; this remains an originality risk.

Earlier interval results cover its N-prime nonuniformity corollary but not its composite-N counts, while the pooled 2023 theorem neither gives nor rules out the per-r statement. An unstated general elementary-symmetric-function identity may imply the formula and would supersede originality; no such result was located.

originality.rationale: Specific implication comparisons were made against the complete relevant part of the 1994 full paper on fixed-cardinality *initial-interval* subset sums and the 2023 full article on *pooled* nonempty unit-subset sums. The proposed theorem identifies a different arithmetic family and supplies an exact signed, positive coefficient for every prime projection at every cardinality; an instance where divisibility is satisfied but uniformity is excluded further distinguishes its content. No equivalent exact formula appeared in the accessible searches . Prime-N nonuniformity was already implied by the 1994 theorem, and possible unindexed general Fourier-enumerator coverage remains a real residual risk.
residual_risks: A general previously published character-enumerator or Ramanujan-sum formula, not recovered by the focused searches, may imply the coefficient identity without explicitly naming this family.

The prime-modulus nonuniformity corollary is implied by Wagon and Wilf (1994); originality is restricted to all-moduli exact two-level prime-projection multiplicities and the strict all-cardinality consequence.
The Hamidoune (1994) full text was not available for direct inspection; its abstract suggests a distinct existential question.
No independent bibliographic or mathematical review has yet been performed.

value.rationale: The classical question of equal distribution for fixed-size subset sums is sharpened for the full reduced residue system, which is a canonical multiplicative-arithmetic set. The exact integer bias coefficient determines both the direction and size at every cardinality for all primes dividing any modulus, and proves an infinite no-uniformity classification. The nonempty cardinality-pooled uniformity for odd N makes the result a distinct structural layer, and at \(N=21,r=6\) it excludes uniformity even though the total subset count is divisible by the modulus. The formula does not merely recalculate a known table or rephrase a type/normalization condition; it identifies an exact natural invariant.
